claim_verdicts.evidence: RFC 9110 §15: "There are five values for the first digit: 1xx (Informational): The request was received, continuing process; 2xx (Successful) ...; 3xx (Redirection) ...; 4xx (Client Error) ...; 5xx (Server Error)". 1xx is the interim class; the lesson says so and leaves it out.
RFC 9110 §15: "a client MUST understand the class of any status code, as indicated by the first digit, and treat an unrecognized status code as being equivalent to the x00 status code of that class."
RFC 9110 §15.3.1: "The 200 (OK) status code indicates that the request has succeeded. The content sent in a 200 response depends on the request method." Table row GET: "the target resource".

§15.3.2: "the request has been fulfilled and has resulted in one or more new resources being created." §9.3.3: "the origin server SHOULD send a 201 (Created) response containing a Location header field".
§15.3.5: "the server has successfully fulfilled the request and that there is no additional content to send in the response content."

§15.4.2: "assigned a new permanent URI ... The server SHOULD generate a Location header field in the response containing a preferred URI reference for the new permanent URI." §15.4.3: "resides temporarily under a different URI ... The server SHOULD generate a Location header field".

§15.4.5: "a conditional GET or HEAD request has been received ... the client, which made the request conditional, already has a valid representation; the server is therefore redirecting the client to make use of that stored representation"; "A 304 response is terminated by the end of the header section; it cannot contain content or trailers."

§15.5.1: "cannot or will not process the request due to something that is perceived to be a client error". §15.5.2: "lacks valid authentication credentials ... The server generating a 401 response MUST send a WWW-Authenticate header field". Caddyfile@stage-0 /admin: respond "Unauthorized: sign in at /login.html first" 401, no header directive.

§15.5.4: "the server understood the request but refuses to fulfill it". §15.5.5: "did not find a current representation for the target resource or is not willing to disclose that one exists". §15.5.10: "could not be completed due to a conflict with the current state of the target resource." The cancel example fits.

§15.6.1: "encountered an unexpected condition that prevented it from fulfilling the request". §15.6.3: "while acting as a gateway or proxy, received an invalid response from an inbound server". §15.6.4: "currently unable to handle the request due to a temporary overload or scheduled maintenance".

RFC 9112 §4: "The reason-phrase element exists for the sole purpose of providing a textual description associated with the numeric status code ... A client SHOULD ignore the reason-phrase content because it is not a reliable channel for information". Lesson "may ignore" is weaker than SHOULD, still true.
§15.5.4: "An origin server that wishes to "hide" the current existence of a forbidden target resource MAY instead respond with a status code of 404 (Not Found)."

§15.5.2: "The user agent MAY repeat the request with a new or replaced Authorization header field". §15.5.4: "the server considers them insufficient to grant access. The client SHOULD NOT automatically repeat the request with the same credentials."

Execution: -w "%{http_code}  $path\n" printed 200/302/404/401/409/503/404, each matching the status line of the response; against a closed port it printed 000. No curl key in versions.yaml; evidence is execution only.

Execution: curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null .../redirect printed header lines only; curl -s alone against a closed port printed nothing (exit 7), -sS printed "curl: (7) Failed to connect". grep -Ei '^(HTTP/|Location:)' on "location: /x","LOCATION: /y","http/1.1 200","X-Location: z" kept the first three only.

status-codes.sh@stage-0 line 5: [ -f /.dockerenv ] || exec "$(dirname "$0")/../lab-run.sh" "$0" "$@". lab-run.sh@stage-0: exec docker compose exec -T lab bash -c 'exec bash "$0" "$@" 2>&1' "/repo/$rel". Code block matches the file at stage-0 (diff empty, 23 lines).

§15: status code is "a three-digit integer code that describes the result of the request"; §15.3.1: 200 "indicates that the request has succeeded". Nothing in §15 derives the code from the content. The recommendation is labelled opinion.

Run: bash -c 'set -euo pipefail; for p in /index.html /x; do curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}  $p\n" http://localhost:9; done 2>&1; echo notreached' printed "curl: (7) Failed to connect ... Could not connect to server" then "000  /index.html", exit 7, no "notreached". web uses network_mode service:lab, so stopping only web closes localhost:8080 in the box. Whole lab down: lab-run.sh fails at docker compose exec.

Opinion grounded in §15.6.3 ("while acting as a gateway or proxy, received an invalid response from an inbound server") and §15.6.4, which defines 503 for "the server" with no intermediary, so a proxy can originate it. Matches the new outline item 4.
§15.5.5: a 404 is what "the origin server" answers when it "did not find a current representation". Execution: with no listener, curl exits 7 and no status line arrives (http_code 000).
§15.5: "The 4xx (Client Error) class of status code indicates that the client seems to have erred." The lesson hedges with "seems" and "usually".

§15.4 lists "Redirects that indicate this resource might be available at a different URI, as provided by the Location header field, as in ... 301 (Moved Permanently), 302 (Found)" and "Redirection to a previously stored result, as in the 304 (Not Modified) status code."

issues.text: The diagram labels every 2xx as "Done". RFC 9110 §15 defines 2xx as "successfully received, understood, and accepted", and §15.3.3 says 202 means "accepted for processing, but the processing has not been completed". A junior who later meets 202 (and a client applying the x00 rule) reads "done" too strongly. The prose ("the request succeeded") is right; only the diagram node overstates.
issues.quote: D -->|2| A["Done. What you asked for is in the body, or there was nothing to send"]
issues.fix: Change the node text to "Succeeded. What you asked for is in the body, or there was nothing to send". No other change; summary line 1 follows outline wording and may stay.

issues.quote: `-w` sets what `curl` prints after each request, `-sS` hides its progress output but keeps error messages, and `%{http_code}` is the numeric code of the answer `curl`, the program that sends the request, received; the body is thrown away.
